name: Refract Erranta
geological_features: Fractured ice crust with exposed crystalline strata
Sublimation jets active during perihelion approach
Cryovolcanic vents along tidal stress fractures
specific_features: A highly eccentric orbit carrying it from the outer system to within the habitable zone, producing a dramatic comet-like coma during close approach
Surface ice sheets that refract starlight into prismatic displays visible from neighboring worlds during perihelion
A trail of sublimated debris stretching millions of kilometers along its orbital path
resources: Frozen volatiles including ammonia and methane
Cometary dust particulates rich in organic precursors
description: Refract Erranta is less a planet than a wanderer — a small ice body locked into a wildly eccentric orbit that carries it from the frozen dark of the outer system to a blazing perihelion pass that skirts the inner habitable zone. At aphelion, it is a silent sphere of nitrogen ice and frozen methane, dark and unremarkable. At perihelion, it transforms into something extraordinary as solar heating drives sublimation jets that wrap the body in a luminous coma hundreds of thousands of kilometers across.

During close approach, the surface ice refracts concentrated starlight into prismatic fans of color that have been observed from neighboring worlds with the naked eye. The effect earned the body its name — early astronomers in the system recorded it as a periodic apparition of fractured light, not recognizing it as a planetary body for decades. The sublimation tail it leaves behind is a river of glittering particulates that takes years to disperse.

The orbit itself is a puzzle. Dynamical models cannot reproduce it through natural gravitational perturbation alone, suggesting either a recent catastrophic interaction with a now-absent massive body or an origin outside the system entirely. Isotopic analysis of captured tail material shows ratios inconsistent with the local stellar nebula, lending weight to the interstellar capture hypothesis. If confirmed, Refract Erranta would be one of the few verified extrasystem bodies in the catalogued territories.

Water ice of Refract Erranta's purity commands premium prices on stations throughout the sector, and its perihelion passes draw ice-mining operations that race to harvest before the body swings back into the dark. The work is dangerous — sublimation jets can erupt without warning, and the body's low gravity makes anchoring equipment a constant challenge. There is also the unresolved question of what happens when the orbit eventually degrades enough to send Refract Erranta spiraling into the inner system permanently.
